question: Why did a released native transport URL sometimes reach the provider (1 request) and sometimes not (0)?
cause: WebCore reuses a same-document image from its memory cache (CachedImage::canSkipRevalidation, CachedImage.cpp:819-821, the per-document image list) while the CachedImage is still cached. Once the image loader releases its element and memory release prunes the clientless CachedImage, the reload misses and reaches the provider.
probe: memory-cache-probe.py on C:/wk/h05-private/native22-final (WebCore babc8278, Host 153db475), 10 rounds per mode

reading.retained/released/purged: 0 requests in every round, decode SUCCEEDED 3x2: memory-cache hits while the element or its loader still holds the CachedImage
reading.evicted: 1 request in every round after 3x(cycle 50ms + GC) then rv_release_memory: misses after pruning
reading.navigated: 1 request in every round: a new document has no per-document reuse

fixture: Engine.ReleaseEngineCaches runs the evicted sequence natively before the reload, so the native fixture expects exactly 1 request; Chromium expects 0 (revoked object URL) with a no-op release.
runs: NativeAOT 5/5 and JIT 3/3 at 29 assertions, Chromium 29; before-fix logs kept (2 of 3 AOT runs got 0 requests).
